# Test fixtures

`data/` follows the layout in `docs/design.md`, so the models read it the same way they read the real `data/` folder. Tests never touch the network.

## Source and extract date

- `data/informacao_base/XVII/`: InformacaoBase XVII (`InformacaoBaseXVII_json.txt`), downloaded from parlamento.pt on 20 Oct 2026. The extract date is **2026-10-19**: AR writes it as the end date of every open group membership, and `legislatures.extract_date` reads it from there.
- `data/registo_biografico/XVII/`: shape taken from RegistoBiografico XVII, downloaded the same day. The content is synthetic (see below).
- `data/iniciativas/`, `data/atividades/XVII/` and `data/informacao_base/XIV/`: Iniciativas XIV, XVI and XVII, Atividades XVII and InformacaoBase XIV, downloaded from parlamento.pt on 20 Oct 2026 in a full sync. These files carry no extract date; the newest vote in Iniciativas XVII is dated 2026-10-16. Used by the initiatives and votes marts.
- `data/iniciativas/I-B/` and `data/informacao_base/I-B/`: Iniciativas I-B and InformacaoBase I-B from the same full sync. Used for the I-B `PPD` to `PSD` alias.
- `data/informacao_base/II/` and `data/registo_biografico/II/`: InformacaoBase II and the RegistoBiograficoII file listed on the AR I Legislatura page, downloaded on 20 Oct 2026. The biographies are synthetic (see below).
- `data/intervencoes/XVII/` and `data/perguntas_requerimentos/XVII/`: Intervencoes XVII and PerguntasRequerimentos XVII from the full sync of 20 Oct 2026 (fetch date 2026-10-20 in the lock). Free text is synthetic (see below).
- `data/_meta/sources.lock.json`: the lock entries for those two files, with `records` set to the trimmed counts and the hash and size left out, since they belong to the full download.

## How they were built

1. One table per file: `CirculosEleitorais`, `DetalheLegislatura`, `GruposParlamentares`, `SessoesLegislativas` and `Deputados` each became an NDJSON file with sorted keys, records in natural-id order.
2. `deputados.ndjson` is trimmed from 1,446 to 298 people: the 288 who held any situation other than Suplente in XVII, plus the first 10 by `DepCadId` who were only ever Suplente. Every seated deputy is kept, so the seat and group counts are the real ones.
3. `registo_biografico/XVII/<id // 1000>/<id>.json`: 5 records for people in `deputados.ndjson`, scalar fields only, pretty-printed with sorted keys. The ids, the key sets (some records lack some keys), the float ids, the null fields and the sex values are as published. Names, birth dates and professions are made up: names start with `Pessoa Sintética` and birth dates are in 1900. A test enforces this.
4. `iniciativas/<legislature>/<id // 1000>/<id>.json`: 9 initiative records as published, picked for the vote cases the tests pin: named dissenters with a count (XVII 356457, 315881), a unanimous vote with no detail (XVII 356774), a unanimous vote whose detail only lists an absent group (XVII 346027), a vote with no detail (XVII 377296), a XVI initiative voted in XVII (XVI 314565), and one vote published on two initiatives (XIV 45682 and 45634, vote 90081). The two XIV records are trimmed: events carrying any other vote are removed, so no XIV vote needs the seated groups of a day.
5. `atividades/XVII/AtividadesGerais.Atividades.ndjson`: 5 of the activity records with votes, as published: two with a detail, two unanimous with no detail (one listing an absent group) and one motion with no detail.
6. `informacao_base/XIV/`: `detalhe_legislatura.ndjson` and `grupos_parlamentares.ndjson` in full, and `deputados.ndjson` trimmed to the 8 deputies who author the two XIV initiatives and the 2 non-inscribed deputies named in vote 90081. These are InformacaoBase records (names, groups, situations), not biographies.
7. `intervencoes/XVII/records.ndjson`: trimmed from 81 to 15 records: 11 deputy interventions picked for variety (type, role, with and without initiatives and audiovisual data) and 4 by government members, plus one empty record with every key null, the shape AR publishes 113 times across V, XI, XIV, XV and XVI. Every speaker is in `deputados.ndjson`.
8. `perguntas_requerimentos/XVII/records.ndjson`: trimmed from 4,076 to 24 records picked for variety: perguntas and requerimentos, recipient categories AC, AL and EI, one or many authors, one or two recipients, with and without answers and extensions. Every author is in `deputados.ndjson`.
9. In both files (items 7 and 8), ids, dates, types, deputy and government member names and ids, groups and recipient bodies are as published: they are public office data. Free text that can name private citizens or companies is made up: summaries, abstracts, debate titles, subjects, notes and related activity titles contain `sintético` or `sintética`, and document, diary, video and answer links point to `https://app.parlamento.pt/fixture/`. A test enforces this.
10. One synthetic value: question 187751 has `DataEnvio` set to `2125-06-12` (published as `2025-06-12`), a year typo of the kind AR publishes in X and XIII, so the invalid sent date rule has a case.
11. Committee votes (#21): `iniciativas/XVII/377/377270.json` (a unanimous committee vote with no detail) and `iniciativas/XVII/315/315661.json` (a committee vote with a detail), trimmed: events carrying plenary votes are removed, so the plenary counts pinned by the #6 tests stay the same. `composicao_orgaos/XVII/Comissoes.ndjson` holds the one committee they were voted in (id 8448), as published in ComposicaoOrgaos XVII on 20 Oct 2026: member names, groups, situations and meetings, which are public office data.
12. `informacao_base/II/`: `detalhe_legislatura.ndjson` as published, and `deputados.ndjson` trimmed from 440 to 3 people (`DepCadId` 4, 5 and 312), as published: public office data. 312 is one of the 8 II deputies with no record in the RegistoBiografico II file.
13. `registo_biografico/II/0/<id>.json`: records for 4 and 5 in the older XML-converted shape (camelCase keys, string `cadId`), scalar fields only. Ids and sex are as published. Names, birth dates and professions are made up as above; 5 has no birth date, as for most II records. The same test enforces this.
14. `iniciativas/I-B/33/33171.json`: one I-B initiative as published. `PPD` is one of its author groups and is listed in its one vote (48952, unanimous with a detail), so the alias seed has a fixture case. `informacao_base/I-B/`: `detalhe_legislatura.ndjson` and `grupos_parlamentares.ndjson` in full (the group list has `PSD`, not `PPD`), and `deputados.ndjson` trimmed to the 10 deputies who author 33171 (12 rows, since some have two `DepId`). These are InformacaoBase records, not biographies.
15. `registo_interesses/<legislature>/records.ndjson` (#8): synthetic records in the four published shapes, one file per shape, with the keys, nesting and value types of the 20 Oct 2026 files: `Constituinte` (V3, people only, like Constituinte to X), `XI` (V1, activities as one free-text field), `XII` (V2, one person with two versions of a declaration), `XIV` (V3 with `RecordInterests`, a V3 person with none, and a V5 form) and `XV` (V5 with nothing declared but exclusivity). The ids are `DepCadId` values from `informacao_base/XVII/deputados.ndjson`; every name, entity and free-text value is made up (`Pessoa Sintética`, `sintético`, `sintética`), and spouse fields are empty. A test enforces this.
16. `ept/getdeclaration.json` (#44): one synthetic EpT `getdeclaration` response with the keys, nesting and tab 4 section and column GUIDs of the 20 Oct 2026 API. Every name and value is made up (`Pessoa Sintética`, `sintético`, `sintética`). It has no `nif` key and no 9-digit value. The tests plant the holder NIF and the entity NIF/NIPC values at runtime: synthetic valid company NIPCs that must be kept, and personal-range values, other 7x prefixes and wrong check digits that must be dropped. They are repeated digit patterns with the check digit computed, never real numbers. A test fails if any fixture under `ept/` holds a `nif` key or a 9-digit value.
